events.content: #1000 merged to main at 11:53Z, restoring Python CI to green
Another agent independently shipped the same P0 fix via PR #1000, built from the dead P0 subagent's worktree branch with identical commit messages.

Review of #1004 found two P2 findings: the cid[:8] point-ID labels are indistinguishable within ~2-month windows, and test_context_free_produces_consistent_ranking remained vacuous behind a None guard.
Decision to fix the P0 CI-red failures by migrating 11 EP tests to status='live' and adding a non-silent degenerate-operator warning, preserving the production draft-filter semantics.
Targeted test runs post-rebase verified all 11 originally-red tests pass, despite extreme I/O contention (load 175-238) from wedged full-suite runs.
User directed that an issue be filed in agent-infra for the subagent stall-at-300s pattern.

points.content: Preserving production behavior is a durable constraint: the draft-filter is correct for production, and the P0 CI-red failure was caused by tests using status='draft'.

The fix approach (migrating 11 EP tests to use status='live' + adding non-silent warning) was optimal because the alternative of changing production draft-filter semantics would violate the durable constraint of preserving production behavior.
The draft-filter's silent degeneration is a known failure mode (#780) that must be diagnosed, not silenced.
Point IDs are ULID-style (<hex-timestamp>-<uuid12>), so cid[:8] is a timestamp prefix shared by all points in a ~2-month window, making labels identical and insufficient for disambiguation.
Concurrent test DB writes from multiple agents cause FalkorDBLite file-lock contention, wedging pytest processes in uninterruptible I/O wait.
The text-first pattern (emit text before any tool calls) defeats the subagent stall under load in this environment.

Subagents stall at the 300s parent-turn bound under load (pattern: alive, working, but never delivers first message within window), believed caused by I/O saturation from 5+ concurrent agent sessions running full test suites (load reached 230).

The migrated test_context_free_produces_consistent_ranking in test_decide.py was vacuous: its assertion block was gated behind a None guard that always skipped the guard body, so the test passed without checking anything.
Targeted test runs post-rebase verified all 11 originally-red tests pass, despite the environment's extreme I/O contention (load 175-238) from multiple wedged full-suite runs.
PR #1004 was ready to merge as-is with no blocking review findings.
